title: nexus verify --json output v2
description: Generated from VerifyJsonOutput in cli/src/verify_contract.ts by cli/scripts/gen_verify_result_schema.mjs. Do not edit by hand. The one JSON document `nexus verify --json` writes to stdout and `--receipt` writes to a file; `schema_version` is its first member.

errorCount.description: Located errors on the base; present when the base run can serve as a baseline.

status.description: NOT_RUN: discovery already ruled the project out (skipped, or its tool is missing).

baselineErrorCount.description: Errors the baseline run (before the change) already had.

enforced.description: False when the result is recorded only (operator-configured verifier, or NEXUS_TYPECHECK mode "record").

excerpt.description: Redacted, control characters made visible, capped, and fenced as untrusted compiler output.

introducedCount.description: Errors in the run that the pre-change baseline run did not have (present only when a baseline was captured).

projects.description: Per-project evidence when a workspace contains multiple configured type-check projects.

scope.description: What the result holds for: "under <configPath>", never universal.

shellChangedFiles.description: Files counted as modified that no edit tool touched (changed through the shell), when any.

status.description:
ENVIRONMENT: the check could not run or be attributed here (not a candidate failure). PREEXISTING: errors exist, but
none in a file the candidate modified; it is not a pass and does not block.

toolSha256.description: Hash of the resolved tool launcher.

command.description: The verifier actually selected: configured override or one discovered from repository files.

deadlineSecs.description: Deadline the verifier was given, recorded when it timed out.

definitionBound.description:
False when the workspace-resolved verifier definition could not be bound before the work (for example a
node_modules tree under `npm test`), so no pass can be independent evidence. The turn is then at most REGRESSION_FREE.

filtered.description: True when the selected test command includes a filter and therefore cannot stand for the full suite.

independent.description:
A discovered verifier's pass is independent evidence of the change: tests that existed before it, unmodified,
failed before and pass after. False (with independenceDetail) when only the agent's own tests, or tests that also
passed before, check it — the turn is then REGRESSION_FREE, not VERIFIED.

typecheck.description: Type-check run beside the verifier. A scoped fact about the named configuration, never about the code in general.

failed.description: The verifier failed on the base tree.

testFiles.description: Test files captured from the base tree; null when one was too large to capture.

usable.description: The base run can serve as the "failed before" half: it failed, by itself, with tests that ran.

verifierDefinitionBound.description: The files that define the verifier were captured from the base tree.

verifierUnbindableReason.description: Why they could not be captured.

VerifyGuard.description: The verification-file guard: which changed files define or weaken the verification, under the BASE tree's policy.

complete.description: False when a changed file could not be classified (unreadable, too large, or too many findings).

mode.description: `approve`: a finding that requires approval blocks until approved. `block`: it blocks, and approval is not accepted.

policySource.description: `base_tree`: the base tree's `.nexus-security.json` (it can only tighten). `default`: the base tree has none. The head's is never read.

status.description: NOT_RUN: verification stopped before the change was read. CLEAR: nothing waits for a decision. BLOCKED: a finding does, or the scan is incomplete.

VerifyGuardFinding.description: One changed file that decides how the change is verified.

approved.description: The operator approved this path. Approval lets the verdict be reported; it never makes the change VERIFIED.

requiresApproval.description: The edit needs `--approve-verification-edit <path>`: a verification configuration file, or a weakened test.

weakening.description: For a test file: what the edit removed (a heuristic over the text). Absent when nothing was detected.

VerifyIngredient.description: An ingredient of the verdict that this version does not run. Later versions add statuses and members.

VerifyJsonError.description: Printed instead of a result when no verdict was reached: a usage error or an interruption.

schema_version.description: Version of this document's schema. Always the first member.

VerifyJsonOutput.description: The one JSON document `nexus verify --json` writes to stdout. A result has `verdict`; an error document does not.

VerifyJsonResult.description: Printed when verification reached a verdict, whatever the verdict. It is also the receipt.

base.description: Absent when the checkout was refused before anything was resolved.

changedFiles.description: Paths that differ between base and head (at most 200 are listed).

environment.description: Names (never values) of verdict-affecting environment variables that were set.

linkedDependencyDirs.description: Dependency directories of the caller's checkout that were linked into both scratch trees.

reason.description: Absent only when the verdict is VERIFIED.

runs.description: Every verifier process that ran, in order.

sandbox.description: Always written; absent only in a document from before `--sandbox` existed (nothing was sandboxed).

schema_version.description: Version of this document's schema. Always the first member.

verification.description: The evidence the outcome was derived from.

timeoutSecs.description: Deadline of each verifier run, and of the type-checks of each side, in seconds.

VerifyReason.description: Why the verdict is not VERIFIED: the outcome ladder's reasons, and the ones only `nexus verify` gives.

executedTests.description: The output shows at least one test that ran.

exitCode.description: Null when the process was killed or never started.

outputTail.description: The end of the output of a run that did not pass: repository-controlled text, redacted and capped.

phase.description: `base_tests_on_head`: the test files as they were on the base, run against the head's code.

sandboxed.description: The process ran inside the sandbox named in `sandbox.engine`. Always written; absent only in a document from before `--sandbox` existed (the run was not sandboxed).

testFixtureReads.description: Baseline test-oracle files opened more often by this candidate run than by the base run. Such a pass is not independent.

VerifySandbox.description:
How the processes `nexus verify` started on repository content were confined: the verifier on each side, the base's
tests against the head, and the type-checks. One answer for all of them: a run is never started outside a sandbox
that was requested.

engine.description: The engine every process ran in. `none`: no sandbox (not requested, or requested and unavailable, in which case nothing ran).

network.description: The confined processes could use the network (`--sandbox-network`). Always false when `engine` is `none`: an unconfined process has the caller's network, which this member does not describe.

requested.description: The operator explicitly selected a sandbox; the effective engine and run records also show default confinement.

commit.description: The commit; null for the working tree, which has none.

ref.description: What the operator named: a ref, or "(working tree)".

tree.description: The Git tree that was materialised and verified. For the working tree: tracked and untracked files that are not ignored, as `git add -A` would stage them (Nexus's own `.nexus` state left out).

VerifyTypecheck.description:
The project type-checks. The evidence of every project (tool, configuration, status, counts, tool hash) is in
`verification.typecheck.projects`; this is the summary and the base side.

baseline.description: The same projects on the base tree: what a "new" error on the head is measured against.

missingFromHead.description: Projects of the base tree that the head no longer has (tool and configuration path).

mode.description: `enforce`: a failing check lowers the verdict. `record`: recorded only (your own `--verifier`). `off`: disabled by NEXUS_TYPECHECK.

status.description:
NOT_RUN: the verifier did not pass on the head (or verification stopped earlier), so no type-check was run.
Otherwise the combined status of the head's projects, as in `verification.typecheck.status`.

VerifyVerdict.description:
VERIFIED: evidence independent of the change shows it. REGRESSION_FREE: the tests pass, which shows only that nothing
they cover broke. UNVERIFIED: nothing was established (see `outcome` and `reason`). BLOCKED: a person must decide
before anything is run or concluded.

approval.description: How it was approved: it is the operator's own command, `--yes`, a matching `--approve-verifier` digest, or not at all.

digest.description: sha256 of the command and the script body it resolves to in the base tree.

evidence.description: The base-tree file that justifies a discovered verifier, or "configured".

script.description: The script body the command resolves to in the base tree (capped), when there is one.

source.description: `configured`: the operator's `--verifier`. `discovered`: selected from the files of the base tree.
